newsitem.title: CHINA: China H1 foreign investment down 48.76 pct.
newsitem.headline: China H1 foreign investment down 48.76 pct.

text.p: Contracted foreign investment in China totalled $23.3 billion in the first half of this year, plunging by 48.76 percent compared with the year-ago period, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Direct investment in the same period reached $20.7 billion, climbing 5.49 percent compared with a year-ago, the newspaper said quoting figures from the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
However, the decline was not a cause for concern, the newspaper said.
"It really should be seen as a normal thing," the newspaper quoted Zhang Shangtang, vice chairman of the China Association of Enterprises with Foreign Investment.
While the number of foreign-funded projects approved in the first half had declined, the size of per project investment had increased, the newspaper said.
China aproved 9,763 foreign-funded enterprises in the first six months, down by 30.5 percent compared with last year, the newspaper said.
However per-project investment averaged $2.12 million, compared with $1.7 million last year and $1.0 million in 1995, it said.
"It's not justifiable for China to always run on the fast track after being the world's second largest investment target for four consecutive years," Zhang said.
Actual foreign investment in China was about $40 billion last year.

The newspaper quoted one economist as saying the high base rate after rapid growth in foreign investment in the first half of this year was partly the cause of the percentage drop in investment in the first six months of this year.
Officials have said they expect actual foreign investment this year to be between $30 billion and $40 billion.
